source: Greiner, Smith, Wilkerson (1989) A correction to the algorithm in Reiter's theory of diagnosis
finding: Reiter's published hitting-set tree algorithm was wrong. Its pruning could lose minimal hitting sets, so diagnoses could be missed. The bug came from the trick used to accept non-minimal conflicts.
numbers: Counterexample collection {a,b},{b,c},{a,c},{b,d},{b} where the pruned HS-tree loses a hitting set. Fix is HS-DAG (reuse nodes; a graph, not a tree).
quote: Reiter's description of the algorithm is incorrect in that some diagnoses can be missed under certain conditions.
limits: Short note: one counterexample and a proof of the fix; no timing data.
agent_relevance: Test any candidate-pruning step for completeness on small cases. Early pruning can silently drop the true culprit.

source: Greiner, Smith, Wilkerson (1989): Reiter versus de Kleer and Williams on conflict minimality
finding: Reiter's method accepts non-minimal conflicts. GDE (de Kleer and Williams) requires the inference engine to hand it minimal conflicts. The theorem: a set is a diagnosis iff it is a minimal hitting set of the conflicts.
numbers: Reiter 1987 Theorem 4.4 as restated; no experiment.
limits: Theory restatement only.
agent_relevance: Failing outputs from our checker will not be minimal. Shrink each conflict to the steps actually needed for the failure before using it, or use the corrected HS-DAG logic.

source: Gainer-Dewar and Vera-Licona (2016) The minimal hitting set generation problem: algorithms and computation
finding: Survey and benchmark of about twenty minimal hitting set algorithms. Confirms Reiter's HS-tree is incomplete (fixed by HS-DAG). MMCS, RS and HTC-BDD are far faster than the others.
numbers: HTC-BDD 4x to 10x faster than its closest rivals on many inputs but often ran out of 32 GB memory. MMCS and RS use little memory and support a size cutoff (tested cutoffs 5, 7, 10). One input had about 500 sets but about 128 million minimal hitting sets.
limits: Inputs are mostly biology and data-mining families, not diagnosis conflicts. Complexity of generation is still an open problem.
agent_relevance: Candidate counts can explode even with few conflicts. Use a small-fault-count cutoff as a default budget.

source: Gainer-Dewar and Vera-Licona (2016): Berge baseline
finding: The classic incremental Berge algorithm is not output-polynomial, even with the best edge order (Takata). The order of conflicts changes the cost a lot.
numbers: Runtime O(k*m*n*min(m,k)), k = largest intermediate collection.
limits: Worst-case result; typical cases may be easier.
agent_relevance: Process small conflicts first and cap candidate count.

source: Gainer-Dewar and Vera-Licona (2016): cardinality-bounded search
finding: Restricting to hitting sets of size at most k is a simple, supported way to cut cost. It matches the usual assumption that few components are faulty at once.
numbers: Cutoff supported in MMCS, RS, Berge, HS-DAG; not in HTC-BDD.
limits: Cutoff loses completeness for larger fault sets.
agent_relevance: Try one-step and two-step fault hypotheses first. Raise the cutoff only if none explains every failure.

source: Stern, Kalech, Feldman, Provan (2012) Exploring the duality in conflict-directed model-based diagnosis
finding: A diagnosis is a hitting set of conflicts, and a conflict is a hitting set of diagnoses. Interleaving the search for both finds minimal-cardinality diagnoses faster than Conflict-Directed A* (CDA*).
numbers: Instances solved under 30 s, CDA* vs new SDE on circuits: c432 33% vs 88%, c499 9% vs 30%, c880 5% vs 14%, c1355 0% vs 9%, 74181 47% vs 79%. The gap grows with diagnosis cardinality.
limits: Circuit benchmarks only. Even the best method solves few large instances in 30 s. Both stages are NP-hard.
agent_relevance: A current best candidate is itself a probe: if it fails to explain a new failure, that failure points to the next conflict.

source: Stern et al. (2012): incompleteness of conflict computation
finding: Conflict-based diagnosis solves two NP-hard problems: minimal conflicts, then minimal hitting sets. Most practical conflict methods are sound but incomplete, and CDA* is not complete. The number of conflicts and diagnoses is exponential in components.
numbers: No experiment; framing section.
limits: Authors' framing of prior work.
agent_relevance: Treat the suspect list as incomplete. Keep a residual 'something else' hypothesis and never claim the culprit from partial conflicts.

source: Shchekotykhin, Jannach, Schmitz (2015) MergeXplain: fast computation of multiple conflicts for diagnosis
finding: A divide-and-conquer method that returns several minimal conflicts per run beats QuickXplain (one conflict per run) when the first few diagnoses are wanted.
numbers: First 5 diagnoses on circuit benchmarks: gain 15% to 45% (c432 707.5 ms vs 503.9 ms). Constraint and spreadsheet problems: up to 54% (costasArray-13), one loss of 11% (queens-8).
limits: Wall time of solver calls. Not tested with a language model.
agent_relevance: If the checker can report several independent failing sets in one pass, take them together instead of one call each.

source: Shchekotykhin et al. (2015) MergeXplain: boundary conditions
finding: The gain depends on where the conflicts sit. When conflicts cluster where QuickXplain searches first, the gain vanishes or reverses. For finding all diagnoses the two are about equal.
numbers: Synthetic, 100 components, 5 conflicts of size 2: Random 54%, Left 33%, Right 14%, Left-and-Right 75%, Neighbours 58%. 50 components, 15 conflicts of size 4, Right: -8%.
limits: Simulated consistency-check cost; real costs vary.
agent_relevance: Batch conflict extraction pays when there are several independent faults. For one fault, a single-conflict search is enough.

source: Peischl and Wotawa (2003) Modeling state in software debugging of VHDL-RTL designs
finding: Consistency-based diagnosis applied to program source. On a small counter with one injected bug, the true bug statement was in the diagnosis set, but so were many other statements.
numbers: Counter example: 25 single-fault and 66 dual-fault diagnoses mapping to 8 statements (10,13,14,15,19,38,40,41). Median single-fault diagnoses on ISCAS85: 1 to 5 on small circuits, 31 on C2670, 306 on C7552.
limits: Hardware-like code, 3 counters. Observations are the user's expected values. C7552 median 122,317 ms, maximum 2,792,591 ms on a 1.8 GHz Pentium 4. Dual faults and time unfolding hit scaling limits.
agent_relevance: The output is a candidate set, not an answer. Rank it and add a discriminating test. One failing test gives wide sets.

source: Peischl and Wotawa (2003): recall versus precision
finding: Diagnosis quality varied with the example and observations used, but the faulty component was always among the diagnoses. Completeness held; precision did not.
numbers: 100 test vectors per circuit, 10 repeats, ISCAS85. Test cases were chosen so at least one single-fault diagnosis exists.
limits: Choosing cases that yield a diagnosis biases results upward. Authors name running time as the obstacle for industrial size.
agent_relevance: Measure both: does the culprit stay in the set, and how many others remain.

source: Abreu, Zoeteweij, van Gemund (2009) Spectrum-based multiple fault localization (BARINEL)
finding: A hybrid of spectrum-based ranking and model-based reasoning. A candidate must explain all failing runs (consistency), then is ranked by Bayesian probability. A cheap heuristic hitting-set step (STACCATO) makes it scale. It typically beats other spectrum methods at slightly higher cost.
numbers: Siemens suite plus gzip, sed, space. Single fault proven optimal. Wasted effort percent, print_tokens with 1, 2, 4 faults: BARINEL 1.2, 2.4, 4.8 vs Tarantula 2.6, 5.3, 11.5.
limits: Gap to Ochiai is small or zero on several programs (print_tokens 5 faults 4.8 vs 4.4; schedule2 near ties). Table layout in the text extract is garbled; read with care. Exact model-based tools handled only the smallest program (tcas).
agent_relevance: A cheap ranking plus a consistency filter is a good middle path between full diagnosis and pure similarity ranking.

source: Abreu et al. (2009) BARINEL: why full MBD does not scale
finding: The authors state MBD is more accurate in principle for multiple faults but needs a model and has exponential candidate generation. Statistical methods assume a single fault.
numbers: BARINEL complexity O(N*M + M log M), the same class as statistical methods.
limits: Authors' framing, supported by their own experiments only.
agent_relevance: Exact diagnosis is not the aim for an LLM agent. Use logic to filter and a cheap rule to order.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are diagnostic concepts within the reach of LLMs?
finding: LLMs were asked to generate Minimal Structurally Overdetermined sets, conflicts and minimal diagnoses for circuits. Reasoning models did surprisingly well but not well enough to replace algorithms.
numbers: o3-mini: conflicts F1 0.917 (sd 0.249), diagnoses F1 0.784 (sd 0.322). Models 4o-mini, o1, o3-mini. Examples hand-made and not in training data.
quote: LLMs do not provide an alternative to diagnosis algorithms.
limits: gpt-4o and 4o-mini scored near zero on unseen examples without code. o1 run once (about 30 USD per iteration); others 10 repeats. Results vary highly between runs and time cannot be bounded.
agent_relevance: Compute hitting sets in code, not in the model. Supports G5.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025): complexity and prompt moderators
finding: Diagnosis generation was the hardest step and degraded clearly as the number of diagnoses grew. A prompt full of domain knowledge and a light prompt gave similar results. Supplying a correct incidence matrix did not help MSO generation much. The apparent rise of conflict F1 with size is an artifact of poor scores on zero-conflict cases.
numbers: Reasoning effort high for the dedicated prompt, medium for the broad prompt. Each step was scored with correct inputs given.
limits: Small hand-made set; scoring each step with correct inputs overstates a full pipeline.
agent_relevance: More domain text is not the lever. Moving the combinatorial step to code is.

source: Karimi Bavandpour and Bercher (2026) LLM-only PDDL domain repair with open-weight models
finding: The symbolic baseline uses conditional hitting sets and returns cardinality-minimal repairs. LLMs exploit names in the model as semantic cues and match the true repair far better, but do not guarantee that all tests pass.
numbers: 12 error-injected IPC domains. Symbolic F1 .49. Best LLM (GLM 5.2, high effort, no traces) F1 .87, mean test-pass rate .82, only .06 on the Thoughtful domain. Best 2025 model F1 .53 vs best 2026 model .85.
quote: repair-set overlap is not a correctness guarantee
limits: Public benchmark, so contamination is possible. The baseline optimizes only size and picks arbitrarily among equal-size repairs; the truth may not be minimal.
agent_relevance: Minimal size is the wrong prior when the real fault is the semantically natural one. Let the model rank, let code verify.

source: Karimi Bavandpour and Bercher (2026): giving failing and passing traces
finding: Adding the test traces did not raise the best result at default effort. It helped only some models at high reasoning effort.
numbers: GLM 5.2 F1 .85 to .78 with traces (default effort). DeepSeek V4 Pro with traces: high effort lifted test-pass rate .82 to .92 and F1 .74 to .82; still .06 on Thoughtful.
limits: Long traces can exceed context. Effect depends on the model. Phi-4 scored F1 0.
agent_relevance: More failure evidence in the prompt is not always better. Condense each failing trace to its minimal conflict.

source: Karimi Bavandpour and Bercher (2026): prompt sensitivity and effort moderator
finding: A shorter prompt without a reasoning request lowered GPT-4o. Higher reasoning effort helps some models and hurts others.
numbers: GPT-4o mean F1 .46 (earlier prompt) vs .38 (short prompt). GPT-OSS-120B high effort: F1 .49 to .15, test rate .57 to .09. GPT-OSS-20B high effort: F1 .23 to .41.
limits: Single run per cell, no confidence intervals.
agent_relevance: Do not assume more thinking helps the conflict step. Test per model and keep a fallback.

source: Sarkar (2026) From errors to proofs: minimal-core-guided repair for neuro-symbolic constraint solving
finding: When the model's formal encoding has no solution, handing it a minimal unsatisfiable core over its own constraints stops a weaker model from dropping real constraints to force an answer.
numbers: 77 problems, 7 domains. Fabricated feasibility on 14 infeasible items: deepseek-v3.2 generic error-message repair 11/14 (79%) vs core repair 1/14 (7%), Fisher p<0.001. gemma4-31b 0% for both.
limits: Strong model shows no gap: core 89.6% vs generic 88.3% accuracy, paired sign test p=1.0. Two open models, one author, 77 items.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for our use. Return the smallest mutually inconsistent set, not a bare failure. The gain appears on weak models.

source: Sarkar (2026): prompting baselines versus the solver route
finding: A strong chain-of-thought prompt matched the symbolic pipeline on accuracy. The value of the solver route is certificates and refusal to fabricate, not accuracy.
numbers: Direct prompting 74.0% and fabricates on 3/14 infeasible (21.4%). Chain-of-thought 98.7%, fabricates none. Pipeline 84.4% first try, 89.6% after repair; repair fixed 4 failures and broke none.
limits: Small scales; chain-of-thought fell to 90% on the largest tier. The pipeline needs several model calls per problem.
agent_relevance: Conflict machinery is not a free accuracy gain at small scale. Justify it by guarantees and equal-token wins (G7).

source: Sarkar (2026): where translation fails
finding: Faulty formalization is concentrated. Local constraints were translated faithfully; global counting (aggregate coverage) was not. A conflict core cannot repair what the model cannot express.
numbers: Six of seven domains faithful; aggregate-coverage scheduling failed even with repair (no-repair 0%).
limits: Fixed prompt; authors say a worked example might narrow the gap.
agent_relevance: Log which kinds of step conflicts cluster on. A conflict that repeats on one pattern signals a model limit, not a one-off slip.

source: Wassermann (2000) Local diagnosis
finding: Consistency-based diagnosis is tied to belief revision: Reiter's algorithm can compute kernel operations, and diagnoses are what to remove to restore consistency. Restricting to the part of the system description relevant to the observation gives smaller conflicts.
numbers: Theory paper, no benchmark numbers.
limits: No empirical evaluation.
agent_relevance: Revising after a contradiction is the same operation as diagnosis. Limit the conflict search to steps connected to the failing output.

source: Roos (2022 posting of 1993 paper) Efficient model based diagnosis
finding: For causal components, a focus on likely broken components and then the most informative probe can be found in O(n^2) worst case, linear when connectivity is low. A conflict set is split by probing a component inside it.
numbers: Worst case O(n^2) in the number of components; linear at low connectivity.
limits: Feed-forward causal systems; the paper reports no benchmark runs.
agent_relevance: In a chain of steps, probe a middle step to halve the conflict set. Cheap and code-driven.

source: Roos (1993) Efficient model based diagnosis: contrast with GDE
finding: Unlike GDE, predictions run in one direction only, which cuts cost but ignores some information. A conflict need not depend on all causal ancestors when a component acts as a switch.
numbers: No measured comparison.
limits: Argument, not experiment.
agent_relevance: Forward re-execution is cheaper than full constraint propagation, and is what a code checker gives us.

source: Reiter (1987) A theory of diagnosis from first principles
finding: Defines a diagnosis as a minimal set of components assumed abnormal that keeps description and observation consistent. Diagnoses are the minimal hitting sets of the conflicts. Original not read; statement taken from Greiner et al. and the duality paper.
numbers: None recorded.
limits: Secondary only.
agent_relevance: Core formalism for S5 localization.

source: de Kleer and Williams (1987) Diagnosing multiple faults
finding: GDE: conflicts via an ATMS, candidates as hitting sets, ranked by prior failure probability. The entropy-based choice of next measurement is from memory only. Original not read.
numbers: None recorded.
limits: Memory and secondary descriptions. Entropy claim unverified this session.
agent_relevance: Source of the idea: pick the next test that best separates the suspects.

source: Pill, Quaritsch, Wotawa (2016) On the practical performance of minimal hitting set algorithms from a diagnostic perspective
finding: Compares complete minimal hitting set algorithms for diagnosis, including the effect of cardinality limits. The PDF download was damaged, so only the abstract was seen via search.
numbers: None.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Open question: which algorithm suits small diagnosis conflict sets.

source: Gap note: LLM agents using Reiter-style conflicts and hitting sets over failed attempts
finding: Searches found a core-guided repair paper, a PDDL repair baseline built on hitting sets and an MSO study. No end-to-end study of conflict plus hitting set over failed code attempts, and no replication of Sarkar 2026, was found.
numbers: None.
limits: Absence in a few searches, not proof of absence.
agent_relevance: This is untested for LLM scaffolds; we need our own test.
